beats.text: The villain is the KV cache, a hoarder forcing your GPU to process irrelevant past frames for every new token.
beats.visual_focus: A bloated cache buffer overflowing with redundant visual data.

beats.text: Velox shatters this by using an attention router that treats video like a camera view, dropping pixels outside the current vision.
beats.visual_focus: A camera frustum slicing through 3D space, isolating relevant tiles.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was solid—calling out the KV cache as a 'hoarder' actually made sense because I've dealt with memory bloat in my own projects. I didn't swipe because you got straight to the point. My only gripe is 'spatial router'—it sounds a bit like a buzzword. I get that you're dropping pixels, but is it a masking layer? A custom attention mask? Just be specific about the implementation.

thriller_metadata.physical_analogy: A hoarder trying to carry every single piece of furniture from a house into a tiny elevator.
thriller_metadata.paradigm_shift: Constant-time generation for infinite-length video rollouts
